output.summary: As a first-time Seat 2 participant, I believe this is a controlled prototype kit for Mandate 2038, version 0.7.0-rc.3-test, with printable component masters plus digital references, manifests, source data, and verification fingerprints. My assigned faction is Kestralyn (vertical_empire), and my decision profile is infrastructure_compounder. I have not read or interpreted the core rules; this record is based only on the supplied kit identity and component inventory.
observedComponents: A Kestralyn player set that should contain: 1 CEO, 3 Teams, 4 double-sided Facilities (normal/Grid-Ready), 1 Generator, an integrated starting-grid identifier on the first Facility, 10 Scrutiny cubes, 1 Customer marker, 1 Escalation marker, 6 Core Action cards, 7 Escalation cards, and 1 double-sided AGI Declaration card.

Equivalent faction component sets appear intended for the other factions in session A: Mirevanta Works, Corthaven, and Loopfold AI. Session B names Dovetalis Labs, Orisonix, and two unspecified returning factions.
A 50-card Training deck: five cards in each of seven domains (35 total), plus 3 Curated Corpus, 3 Licensed Dataset, 3 Benchmark Leak, 3 Synthetic Loop, and 3 Human Evaluation cards.
Headline cards divided into Era decks. The exact physical card count is not stated here; Default Game decks apparently exclude cards bearing an Advanced Play badge.
Era cards and Era Mandate cards, though their exact quantities are not specified in the component reference.
Power Source cards or components, included as a baseline module, with exact quantities not stated.
Reference cards, included as a baseline module, with their exact printed inventory not stated.
Shared contract pieces: 6 numbered matched Joint Venture token pairs and 6 numbered matched Mega-Cluster token pairs; Mega-Cluster pieces include a lead-side indicator.
Shared markers and supplies: 1 Fusion Demonstrator marker, 18 Systemic Risk cubes, 1 opaque Audit bag, and 1 Initiative marker.
Map components and token contracts are included, but the supplied component inventory does not enumerate the map pieces or give a full token count.
Faction boards, apparently including tracks for Customers and Escalation availability.
Printable or production material represented by component-masters.html, with card-reference.md, component-reference.md, and map-reference.md serving as inventory/reference aids.

Administrative and verification material: KIT-LABEL.txt, README.md, playtest-protocol.md, receipt schema, executable and rules-candidate manifests, content manifest, source JSON files, world material, and extensive fingerprints/hashes.
Explicitly absent from this baseline kit: Tactics, secret objectives, and Reserve Specialists. A 36-card Tactic deck is described only as deferred, so I would not expect it in the playable inventory.

output.summary:
Default Game is a four-Era, three-to-five-player game. Highest public Mandate wins; the institutional winner and shared World Ending are resolved separately. Each Era has three simultaneous-selection action cycles followed by Power and Production, Public Audit, and Era Mandate scoring.

Setup: Build the fixed thirteen-tile structure with Frontier at center, a shuffled six-tile operational ring, and six shuffled public tiles in the designated outer positions. Use only Headlines without an Advanced Play badge, separated by Era; shuffle the Training deck; and make four three-card Era Mandate decks. Each faction receives its board, six Core Actions, seven Escalations, CEO, three Teams, four Facilities, one Generator, Declare AGI card, markers, and printed starting resources. Put every CEO and one Team at Frontier, leave two Teams in supply, use all printed Kestralyn starting tracks and already-earned Mandate, and keep all ten Kestralyn Scrutiny cubes outside the initially empty Audit bag. Record Setup Collective Trust from all factions’ printed starting Trust. Choose Initiative randomly. Do not use Tactics or secret objectives.

Turns: At each cycle, reveal and resolve a Headline, then everyone secretly commits one unused Core Action or an unlocked Escalation and reveals simultaneously. Resolve clockwise from Initiative. The acting CEO or Team moves zero to two adjacent hexes, then performs the selected action from its destination; the card is exhausted afterward. A CEO supplies two presence and a Team one. Facilities and Generators never act. Initiative passes clockwise after every cycle. Selection commits only the action; piece, route, target, payment, and any immediate trade are chosen during resolution. If earlier resolution removes every legal target, movement still occurs and the action exhausts without effect or compensation.

Core Actions: Fund gains either two Runway, or four Runway plus two Scrutiny. Research costs one Compute and draws Training cards individually, accumulating provisional Capability from unique domains until banking or crashing on an unprotected duplicate. Safety or one Research Commons visit can protect a duplicate only by discarding it and immediately banking; special Training cards have their printed procedures. Build constructs a Facility for two Runway on the acting piece’s non-Frontier hex, or—starting Era II—one ordinary Generator per player on an Energy hex at its location-defined cost and type. Organize recruits a Team, moves personnel, or relocates a Facility. Deploy costs one Compute, requires Capability thresholds 2/4/6/8/10 for Customers 1–5, gains the Customer, and adds one Scrutiny. Influence performs printed political effects or creates/terminates a Joint Venture.

Resources and scoring: Runway, Compute, and Safety cap immediately at 12, 10, and 3 respectively, except a printed faction Safety limit. Capability is permanent unless a rule instructs spending it. Customers produce one Runway during Production and immediately score Mandate: two each for Customers 1–3 and one each for 4–5. First reaching Capability 3, 6, 9, and 12 normally scores two Mandate each; first reaching Trust 2, 4, and 6 scores two each. Threshold awards are permanent despite later losses. Facilities, control, stored resources, and unused cards have no hidden conversion into Mandate.

Power: Default Game uses local Power. Kestralyn’s dedicated starting grid powers only its marked first Facility, cannot be sold, and does not satisfy Mega-Cluster’s added demand. A Generator can power only Facilities on its hex or adjacent hexes; Facilities do not relay Power. Recalculate connections after movement. Every Facility needs one Power to produce. In Production, all players complete each box before proceeding: Generate, Trade, Allocate, Produce, then Partner. Era III permits one Power purchase request per player in Initiative order to an adjacent rival connection; accepted installed Generator/Fusion Power costs one Runway per unit, and each supplier may sell at most one Power. Starting-grid and emergency Power cannot be sold. Full Power flips a Facility Grid-Ready; loss of full or legal Power flips it back. Purchased Power lasts only for that Production.

Era progression: Era I activates Core Actions, Training, starting grids, Facilities, Customers, and Scrutiny; there is no Escalation availability. Era II grants one availability and unlocks Generators, Mega-Cluster, Reorganization, and Escalations. Era III grants one availability and unlocks Joint Ventures, immediate Power purchases, Open Weights, and Narrative Capture. Era IV grants two availability and unlocks Agent Swarm, Declare AGI, Fusion Demonstrator, and exceptional faction programs. Escalation availability expires at Era end, but unlocked unused Escalation cards remain available; each named Escalation can be used once per player per game.

Contracts and major infrastructure: Joint Ventures require explicit consent, different-player adjacent Facility hosts, an available matched token pair, and both hosts powered during Production. Each partner receives only the resource shown by the contract icon on the other host tile. Mega-Clusters also use matched pairs and adjacent hosts. A solo cluster costs three Runway and two Compute, requires both hosts to be eligible for the owner’s local Power, demands Power for both Facilities plus two more, and produces three Compute. A joint cluster divides construction cost and Power demand between consenting lead and partner and produces two Compute for the lead and one for the partner. Host adjacency must persist. Contracts remain owned but become inactive when requirements fail.

Era IV: Agent Swarm requires two different unused Core Actions, moves once, performs both actions from one destination in either order, applies only one visit bonus, exhausts both actions, and adds three Scrutiny. Declare AGI requires Capability 9+, three Customers, three existing Grid-Ready Facilities, Trust 2+, and three Compute. The first valid declaration scores seven Mandate, later ones five, and each adds three Scrutiny; play continues. A Facility built in Era IV cannot qualify that Era because Grid-Ready status must have been earned in a completed Production. Fusion costs five Runway on Power Corridor, occupies one Generator slot, supplies six Power, scores two Mandate, and adds three Scrutiny; it is separate from the one-ordinary-Generator limit.

Audit: Scrutiny cubes enter the opaque bag when instructed. If all ten Kestralyn cubes are already in it, each additional required cube instead costs one Runway or one Trust when available. Audit draws depend on player count and Era. In Eras I–III, each drawn Kestralyn cube costs one Runway or one Trust; in Era IV it costs two Runway or one Mandate under the stated availability rules. Drawn colored cubes return to their owners; undrawn cubes remain. A drawn black Systemic Risk cube penalizes every player with at least three Customers and returns to supply.

Negotiation and Mandates: During the active player’s turn, immediately before or after Act, one complete Runway/Compute/Safety offer may be made to one rival, with at most one complete counteroffer. Acceptance transfers resources immediately; future promises are nonbinding. Joint projects always require explicit consent. At Era scoring, reveal only one of the three Mandates for that Era. If anyone meets its minimum qualification, the qualifying leader gets two Mandate; tied qualifying leaders get one each. No other criterion breaks that tie.

Endgame: Read the twelve-card Future Timeline, then lose one Mandate per offline Facility. AGI emerges only if at least one declaring institution finishes with Capability 9+. The ending is Open only if final Collective Trust is at least Setup Collective Trust plus player count and unresolved black Systemic Risk in the bag is below player count; otherwise it is Closed. Cross AGI/no AGI with Open/Closed to select the named ending. Highest Mandate wins, with ties broken by Trust, Customers, Compute, then joint victory. No other endgame scoring applies.

For Seat 2 specifically, seat number does not grant a rules privilege in this document. Kestralyn’s printed board and cards are necessary authorities for its starting values, starting Mandate, Safety limit if exceptional, persistent identity, signature program, and other faction modifications. The infrastructure_compounder profile is not assigned any rules effect here.

The universal tie rule targets the tied player nearest Initiative clockwise unless an effect applies to everyone or expressly rewards every tied player.
All cross-player contracts, jointly funded projects, Power sales, and resource trades require explicit acceptance; silence, pass, or timeout means rejection.
Resource caps apply immediately after every gain or trade, and resources cannot pass through an over-cap state.
Cost adjustments apply replacements and waivers first, then surcharges, then discounts; final cost cannot be negative.
A moved Facility retains its starting-grid state and contract/Mega-Cluster tokens, but Power eligibility and contract activity are recalculated immediately.
Grid-Ready is earned only through successful full allocation during completed Production and is lost upon relocation, loss of legal connection, or insufficient Production Power.
An offline Facility still occupies space, contributes presence, and may be visited, but produces nothing and loses one Mandate at game end.

Systems are inactive until introduced by an Era’s New this Era strip; later Eras retain earlier systems unless an effect says otherwise. All Era cards, Escalations, and faction abilities are open information. Reveal one of three Era Mandates each Era and return the other two unseen. Headline effects normally expire at cycle end unless they name that Era’s Production. Exactly three Headlines appear per Era, forming a twelve-card Future Timeline. Setup Collective Trust is fixed from printed starting Trust values and is only used when determining the World Ending. Customers each produce one Runway during Production and score immediate Mandate: two each for Customers 1–3, one each for 4–5. Capability first-time thresholds 3/6/9/12 normally score two Mandate each unless Corthaven says otherwise; Trust first-time thresholds 2/4/6 score two each. Threshold Mandate is never lost merely because the track later falls. Facility construction costs two Runway and requires a non-Frontier destination with an open Facility space; each non-Frontier hex has two such spaces. Facilities cannot be destroyed by rivals. Generator construction unlocks in Era II, requires the acting piece on an Energy hex, and each player may own one ordinary Generator. Energy hexes have three shared Generator slots. Power Corridor builds a one-Runway Emergency Power Complex with four Power and one Scrutiny each Production; Thermal or Water Basin builds a two-Runway Civic Heat Battery with three Power and one Trust on construction. The starting grid supplies one dedicated Power only to the first Facility and cannot be sold. Ordinary Generators and Fusion may sell capacity under the Era III Production trade procedure; each supplier sells at most one Power per Production for one Runway per Power, and only to an adjacent rival Power connection with consent. Purchased Power lasts only that Production. Allocate local capacity only once among legal recipients. Offline Facilities still occupy space, contribute presence, and may be visited, but produce nothing. Powered Facilities produce before Customers, Mega-Clusters, and then Joint Ventures; apply caps after every gain. A moved Facility carries its starting-grid state and contract/Mega-Cluster halves, but immediately recalculates local Power and contract activity. Relocation removes Grid-Ready until a later successful Production. Joint Ventures require explicit consent and two adjacent Facilities owned by different players unless a faction rule changes range. Both hosts must be powered during Production. Each partner gains only the contract-icon resource printed on the other host tile. Influence permits one complete proposal with no substitute partner after rejection, or termination of one named shared Venture. Mega-Cluster construction in Era II costs three Runway and two Compute total, adds two Scrutiny, uses adjacent hosts, and requires the acting piece on either host’s hex. Solo clusters require both Facilities to be eligible for the owner’s local Power; powering both hosts plus two extra demand yields three Compute. Joint clusters divide consent, costs, demand, and output between lead and partner exactly as printed, and stop operating if hosts cease to be adjacent. Reorganization moves all Teams up to one hex; optionally return one Team for three Runway and one Scrutiny. Open Weights gives everyone one Capability and gives its user two Trust plus removal of one Scrutiny. Narrative Capture chooses one printed benefit/attack. Agent Swarm requires two different unused Core Actions, moves once, resolves both at one destination in either order, applies only one visit bonus, exhausts both, and adds three Scrutiny. Declare AGI requires Capability 9+, three Customers, three existing Grid-Ready Facilities, Trust 2+, and spending three Compute at resolution. A Facility built in Era IV cannot support a declaration that Era. First declaration scores seven Mandate; later ones five; each adds three Scrutiny. Play continues afterward and victory does not require AGI. Fusion in Era IV requires ending movement on Power Corridor, five Runway, and an open Generator slot. It provides six Power, scores two Mandate, adds three Scrutiny, and does not consume the owner’s ordinary-Generator limit. Research ordinary domains are Code, Science, Web, Books, Images, Video, and Synthetic. Unique ordinary domains add one provisional Capability. After any non-duplicate, the player may bank or continue. An unprotected duplicate loses provisional Capability, adds Scrutiny, and ends the run; earlier non-Capability effects remain. One Safety or one Research Commons protection can stop a duplicate and bank, but cannot continue. Curated Corpus impersonates an unrevealed ordinary domain; Benchmark Leak adds two provisional Capability and one Scrutiny; Licensed Dataset costs one Runway to continue or banks and stops; the first Synthetic Loop creates unique Loop, and makes the next duplicate unprotectable; Human Evaluation gives one Trust, banks, and stops. Deploy Capability requirements for Customers 1–5 are 2/4/6/8/10. Deploy normally costs one Compute and always adds one Scrutiny; Human Access District waives the Compute cost. Political Influence at the three named spaces gains Trust or removes Scrutiny with location bonuses as printed. It creates no separate presence piece. When all ten Corthaven Scrutiny cubes are already in the bag, each additional required cube instead causes payment of one Runway or loss of one Trust, using the available option; if neither is available there is no further loss, but the risky action otherwise proceeds. In four-player Audits draw 2/3/4/5 cubes in Eras I–IV. Era I–III colored-cube penalties are one Runway or one Trust. Era IV penalties are indivisible: pay two Runway or lose one Mandate; with fewer than two Runway lose Mandate if possible, and at zero Mandate reduce Runway to zero. Systemic Risk cubes penalize every player with at least three Customers using the current Era penalty. Era Mandates use only their printed qualification and criterion. If nobody qualifies, nobody scores; a sole qualifying leader gets two Mandate and tied qualifying leaders each get one. At game end read the Future Timeline, then lose one Mandate per offline Facility without going below zero. AGI emerges only if at least one declarer finishes with Capability 9+. The ending is Open only if final Collective Trust is at least Setup Collective Trust plus player count and unresolved Systemic Risk is below player count; otherwise it is Closed. Cross Open/Closed with AGI emergence/non-emergence to select the named ending. Highest Mandate wins after the offline penalty. Victory ties break by higher Trust, then Customers, then Compute, then joint victory.
crossReferencesNeeded: Corthaven faction board and its matching card faces: printed starting Runway, Compute, Capability, Customers, Trust, Safety, starting Mandate, remaining track markers, Safety cap, persistent identity, signature program, and any scoring/timing/range modifications.

Map reference: exact thirteen-tile identities and ring membership, legal adjacency after assembly, printed location bonuses/effects, Facility spaces, Generator slots, contract icons, presence/control rules, and how the first Facility’s starting-grid assignment is represented.

Card reference or physical cards: exact text for all six Corthaven Core Actions, seven Escalations, four Era cards and their New this Era strips, eligible Default Headlines, Era Mandates, Training cards, and Power Source cards.
Component reference: authoritative deck composition, component limits, marker definitions, ownership markings, matched-token handling, and exact identification of Corthaven’s pieces.
Era reference: where Setup Collective Trust is recorded and any printed Era procedure not reproduced here.

World and Institutions: the narrative for the final shared ending and the winning institution’s ending/history text. It is narrative rather than a scoring authority, but the rules instruct the table to read it. Advanced Play, Balance and Exploitability, and Playtesting and Evidence are not needed for this Default first play.
